prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a landscape 3:2 Minecraft builder reference sheet, crisp vanilla Minecraft voxel blocks only, plain light ivory background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side, LEFT straight-on orthographic front elevation, RIGHT three-quarter view of the identical build at the same block scale. Entire buildings and ground visible. Skilled human builder quality with real massing, proud piers, recessed framed openings, stairs/slabs/fences/walls/trapdoors/lantern detail, actual roof verges, eaves and ridges.
Site: Victorian high-street terrace of exactly three attached red-brick shop-houses on cobblestone and andesite street with pale polished_andesite pavement. Each house exactly 13 blocks wide, total 39 wide; lot 33 deep, buildings 18 deep. Tall shop storey plus two storeys of flats plus gable loft, ridge y25. Each house has its own steep 45-degree grey-slate front gable, three matching sawtooth gables meeting in valleys at party walls. Cream sandstone piers stand one block proud dividing houses and rise to strong sandstone cornices under gables. Sandstone coping edges verges. Wide open shopfront per house under dark-oak fascia: left bookseller blue awning and exact lettering "BOOKS"; middle florist green and pink awning and "FLORA"; right ironmonger red awning and "TOOLS". Use stepped stair and banner awnings. Spruce counters and glass fins behind open fronts. Each fascia has a hanging sign on bracket and lantern beneath awning. Narrow brick bay beside EACH shop holds dark-oak residents' front door, glass fanlight, lantern on each side. Above sandstone string course, each house has THREE recessed window groups per flat floor, centre group triple-width; centre first-floor window has small iron Juliet balcony. Sandstone sills/lintels, grey stone-brick base. One attic window per front gable. Rear brick chimney per house climbs above rear ridge, stone band, slab cap, white campfire smoke. Small brick-walled rear yards with grass and paths, visible as much as camera permits.
Exact block palette by role (use these Minecraft ids; needed stair/slab variants of these materials are allowed; spruce counter components are allowed as specified):
WALLS: bricks, brick_stairs, brick_slab, brick_wall.
TRIM: smooth_sandstone, smooth_sandstone_stairs, smooth_sandstone_slab, cut_sandstone, sandstone_wall.
FASCIA: dark_oak_planks, dark_oak_stairs, dark_oak_slab, dark_oak_door, dark_oak_fence, dark_oak_trapdoor, dark_oak_hanging_sign.
ROOF: cobbled_deepslate, deepslate_tiles, polished_deepslate, polished_blackstone_bricks, stone_bricks, with appropriate stairs/slabs for steep roofs.
BASE: stone_bricks, stone_brick_stairs, stone_brick_slab.
PAVING: polished_andesite.
ROAD: cobblestone, andesite.
GLASS: glass_pane.
SHOP: dark_prismarine_stairs, waxed_oxidized_cut_copper_stairs, red_nether_brick_stairs, quartz_stairs, blue_wall_banner, green_wall_banner, red_wall_banner, white_wall_banner.
PRODUCT: bookshelf, flower_pot, potted_azalea_bush, potted_pink_tulip, anvil, barrel.
GROUND: stone.
YARD: grass_block, coarse_dirt, dirt_path.
Functional/decor: iron_bars, lantern, iron_chain, ladder, hay_block, campfire. Spruce counters: spruce_planks, spruce_stairs, spruce_slab, spruce_trapdoor.
No invented non-Minecraft materials, no smooth realistic geometry. Preserve block grid and restrained Victorian detail. The two views are the focus; no palette swatches or extensive labels needed.
changes: Generated with the built-in image tool and copied without post-processing to concept.png in the current directory.

Raster art does not encode block identities. Added ids identify plausible vanilla equivalents for visible shapes; exact species, wood types, banner construction and hidden blocks cannot be verified. All original palette entries are retained even where not visibly identifiable.

Both views show three shops, two flat storeys and three front gables, but exact 13-block house widths, 39-block total width, 18-block building depth, 33-block lot depth and ridge y25 are not verifiable.
The front elevation is approximately orthographic; identical scale between the two views is not established.
Only the middle house has a Juliet balcony. It is on the upper flat storey, rather than the first floor above the shops.
Centre windows are not consistently triple-width; several window groups appear similar in width.
The continuous sandstone string course between the two flat storeys is missing; individual sills and lintels dominate instead.
The three front gables are present, but the roof behind them reads partly as a connected longitudinal roof; three separate roof valleys over the party walls are not clearly resolved.
The trim includes textured sandstone and cut-looking blocks beyond the supplied smooth-sandstone emphasis.

Awnings have blue/light-blue, green/pink and red/white stripes. Their thin sloping fabric-like edges are not consistently realizable as vanilla stairs or banners; wool and pink-banner equivalents are additions.
Shop lettering and pictorial hanging signs are rendered as graphic details rather than reliably reproducible vanilla sign text or banner patterns.
The narrow residents' door bay is clear beside the middle and right shops in the front view; a separate left-shop residents' door is not clearly shown.
Glass fanlights appear above visible residents' doors, but the specified glass fins behind each open shopfront are not clearly distinguishable.
Added abundant window flowerpots, pavement shrub planters, wooden flower display boxes, storage containers and rear-yard vegetation.
Shop interiors include small tool and merchandise shapes that do not resolve into identifiable vanilla blocks; item frames are plausible equivalents for some displays.
Rear yards and a rear door are visible in the three-quarter view, but all three yard divisions and their planned dimensions are not established.
Three smoking chimneys are visible in the front view; only two are clearly visible in the three-quarter view. Their hidden campfires are inferred from smoke.
The planned hay_block and iron_chain are not clearly identifiable in the image. A ladder-like rear-yard detail is visible.
